external_entities.name: Member
external_entities.description: A person who uses the loyalty programme, mobile app, and partner apps.

external_entities.name: Member phone
external_entities.description: A member's phone hosting the mobile app and its refresh token.
external_entities.source_excerpt: The app keeps a refresh token on the phone.

external_entities.name: Browser
external_entities.description: The browser used for authorization-server sign-in, consent, and redirect handling.
external_entities.source_excerpt: The browser then returns to the partner app's redirect URI with an authorization code.

external_entities.name: Partner company
external_entities.description: A company running a partner application outside the organization's control.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Partner apps are web applications that other companies run on their own servers

external_entities.name: Partner servers
external_entities.description: Servers run by other companies that host partner applications.
external_entities.source_excerpt: other companies run on their own servers

processes.name: Mobile app
processes.description: The mobile application used by members to sign in and call the rewards API.
processes.notes: Nobody wrote down whether the app sends a PKCE challenge.

processes.name: Authorization server
processes.description: The server handling member sign-in, authorization codes, tokens, scopes, and consents.
processes.source_excerpt: The app signs a member in through our authorization server with the authorization code flow

processes.name: Rewards API
processes.description: The API called by the mobile app and used to read and write the points ledger.
processes.source_excerpt: The rewards API reads and writes the points ledger

processes.name: Partner app
processes.description: A web application run by another company that can show a member's points.
processes.source_excerpt: Partner apps are web applications that other companies run on their own servers

processes.name: Support console
processes.description: A web application that closes a member's account.
processes.source_excerpt: The support console is a web app that closes a member's account.

data_stores.name: Identity database
data_stores.description: Stores member accounts, email addresses, password hashes, authorization codes, refresh tokens, and consents.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The authorization server keeps member accounts, email addresses and password hashes in the identity database

data_stores.name: Points ledger
data_stores.description: Stores every member's balance and every points transaction, and records which client made each change.
data_stores.source_excerpt: the points ledger, which holds every member's balance and every points transaction

data_stores.name: API log store
data_stores.description: Stores every request received by the rewards API, including headers.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The rewards API also writes every request it receives, headers included, to the API log store.

data_flows.name: use mobile app
data_flows.description: The member uses the mobile application.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Members use our mobile app.
data_flows.data_description: Member interactions with the mobile app

data_flows.name: authorize member
data_flows.description: The mobile app signs the member in through the authorization server using the authorization code flow.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The app signs a member in through our authorization server with the authorization code flow
data_flows.data_description: Authorization requests, authorization code, access token, and refresh token

data_flows.name: call rewards API
data_flows.description: The mobile app calls the rewards API with an access token.
data_flows.source_excerpt: then calls the rewards API with the access token it gets back.
data_flows.data_description: Access token and rewards API requests

data_flows.name: sign in
data_flows.description: The member signs in on the authorization server's sign-in page in a browser.
data_flows.source_excerpt: A member who connects a partner app signs in on the authorization server's sign-in page in their browser

data_flows.name: authorize partner
data_flows.description: The browser submits sign-in and consent interactions to the authorization server.
data_flows.source_excerpt: signs in on the authorization server's sign-in page in their browser and approves a consent screen

data_flows.name: request tokens
data_flows.description: The partner app makes token requests using its client secret in the request body.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The partner app sends that secret in the body of its token requests.
data_flows.data_description: Client ID, client secret, authorization code, and token requests

data_flows.name: return authorization code
data_flows.description: The browser returns to the partner app's redirect URI with an authorization code.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The browser then returns to the partner app's redirect URI with an authorization code.

data_flows.name: store identity data
data_flows.description: The authorization server stores and retrieves accounts, credentials, codes, tokens, and consents.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The authorization server keeps member accounts, email addresses and password hashes in the identity database, together with the authorization codes, refresh tokens and consents it issues.
data_flows.data_description: Member accounts, email addresses, password hashes, authorization codes, refresh tokens, and consents

data_flows.name: read-write ledger
data_flows.description: The rewards API reads and writes the points ledger.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The rewards API reads and writes the points ledger

data_flows.name: write API requests
data_flows.description: The rewards API writes received requests and headers to the API log store.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The rewards API also writes every request it receives, headers included, to the API log store.

data_flows.name: obtain access token
data_flows.description: The support console takes access tokens from the authorization server.
data_flows.source_excerpt: It takes access tokens from the same authorization server

data_flows.name: close account
data_flows.description: The support console marks a member's account closed in the identity database.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Closing an account marks it closed in the identity database.

trust_boundaries.name: Our cloud account
trust_boundaries.description: The organization's own cloud account where the platform components and stores run.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: Everything below runs in our own cloud account

trust_boundaries.name: Member phones
trust_boundaries.description: The phones used by members, outside the organization's control.

trust_boundaries.name: Partner servers
trust_boundaries.description: Servers operated by other companies that host partner applications.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: other companies run on their own servers

assumptions.assumption: The rewards API is internet-facing because it is served on a public hostname.
assumptions.basis: The support console is served on the same public hostname as the rewards API.

assumptions.assumption: The support console is internet-facing because it is served on a public hostname.
assumptions.basis: The support console is served on the same public hostname as the rewards API.

assumptions.assumption: The identity database has confidential data because it stores member accounts, email addresses, password hashes, authorization codes, refresh tokens, and consents.
assumptions.basis: The source explicitly lists personal data, password hashes, tokens, authorization codes, and consents in the identity database.

assumptions.assumption: The points ledger has confidential data because it stores member balances and points transactions.
assumptions.basis: The source states that the ledger holds every member's balance and every points transaction.

assumptions.assumption: The API log store has confidential data because it stores all requests including headers, which may contain access tokens and personal request data.
assumptions.basis: The source states that every request received by the rewards API, headers included, is written to the API log store.
